properties.endpoint: `reflow2_core::DesignGraph`, linked directly by callers within this workspace. No transport, no wire, no address — it is a Rust library API, which is why `payload_format`, `auth` and `transport_security` are all `none` rather than unspecified: there is no serialization, no principal and no channel, and saying so is a fact about the boundary rather than a gap in describing it.
properties.error_model:
`Result<T, DynoError>`, where `DynoError` is dynograph-foundation's error type — inherited with the payload types rather than defined here.

Absence is not an error: a node that is not there is `Ok(None)`, a type with no nodes is `Ok(vec![])`. An unknown node type IS an error and must not be answered as an empty result — "no such type" and "no such node" are different facts and must not share a reply. `ifc:graph-read` states the same obligation for its subset, and states it in more detail because that one has to survive a second implementation.
properties.name: DesignGraph API
properties.operations:
⚠️ THIS BOUNDARY CANNOT ENUMERATE ITS OPERATIONS, AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING RECORDED ABOUT IT.

`DesignGraph` exposes **277 public functions** across 43 files (measured 2026-08-21), and the number grows whenever anyone adds a method. Its name — "DesignGraph API" — therefore means "whatever that struct happens to expose today". A contract whose scope grows by default is a label on a moving target, not something a second implementation could satisfy or a reader could rely on.

It is recorded here as unenumerable rather than left blank, because blank reads as "nobody got round to it" and the truth is "it cannot be done in this shape".

⭐ THE ONE ENUMERATED SUBSET IS `ifc:graph-read`: five named read operations, where adding a sixth is a deliberate act somebody has to justify. That is what a module can be swapped, tested and measured across — demonstrated on `granularity`, which reads a design made of two Vec's and cannot tell it from a real store. If more of this surface is ever wanted as a real contract, the route is more narrow interfaces like that one, not an attempt to write down all 277.
properties.payload_schema:
The eleven `schema/*.yaml` files, which declare every node type, edge type and property this API reads and writes: build, core, dimensions, environment, functional, inference, operate, readiness, structure, temporal, verify.

They are recorded as such structurally — each carries a `SPECIFIES` edge to this interface with `format: json_schema` — and this field now says the same thing. Until 2026-08-21 it read `unspecified` while those eleven edges asserted the opposite, so the design contradicted itself about whether its own contract was written down.

Values crossing the boundary are `dynograph_storage::{StoredNode, StoredEdge}` and `dynograph_core::Value`, owned Rust values passed in-process. Those types belong to dynograph-foundation (`ifc:req-dyno-storage-api`, designation `required`) and are inherited, not defined here.
properties.spec:
The whole public surface of `reflow2_core::DesignGraph` — the in-process Rust API every module of this crate reads and writes the design through. INTERNAL: reflow2-core is not distributed as a crate, so nothing outside this workspace can link it, and this boundary promises nobody anything. `dec:core-api-withdrawn-from-the-published-surface` records why, and names the two triggers that would reopen it.

IT IS A BOUNDARY THE DESIGN CANNOT FULLY DESCRIBE, and the `operations` field says so at length rather than leaving a blank that would read as unfinished paperwork. 277 public functions, growing by default. The narrow, enumerable subset is `ifc:graph-read`.

A NOTE ON WHY `medium: library` MATTERS AND IS NOT DECORATION: this is linked into its callers rather than called across, so it cannot fail on its own, and the structural detectors need to know that to avoid reporting a linked-in foundation as a single point of failure. It carried `medium: REST` until 2026-07-28 — never chosen by anyone, it arrived as the schema default, and a default that asserts is exactly what `cap:defaults-are-not-serialized` now prevents. That correction is history and lives in the change record and in `snap:epoch:v0380:ifc:core-api`; this field describes the contract.
